column2: On the authority of Ibn Masʿūd (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “The blood of a Muslim person is not lawful except in one of three cases: the married adulterer, a life for a life, and the one who leaves his religion and separates from the community.” Agreed upon (al-Bukhārī and Muslim).

Lā yaḥillu (“is not lawful”): it is not permissible to shed his blood. Imriʾ (“person”): a man. Muslim: a description of the man. Bi-iḥdā thalāth (“in one of three”): qualities. Al-thayyib al-zānī (“the married adulterer”): one who has married and had intercourse within a valid marriage.

“A life for a life”: one who kills deliberately without right is killed. “The one who leaves his religion”: the apostate from the religion of Islam. “Separates from the community”: the community of the Muslims.
The married adulterer is put to death by stoning, as explained in the hadith.
The Arabic of this benefit appears garbled in the edition (في كما بين في حديث); the translation gives its evident sense.
Whoever kills a soul deliberately without right is killed, under the conditions for the death penalty.
It is lawful to kill the apostate from Islam.
Whoever has done none of these three things, his blood is not lawful.

The noble Prophet ﷺ has made clear to us in this hadith that it is not permissible to shed the blood of the Muslims, because their blood is made inviolable by Islam, and that the blood of a Muslim is lawful only if he commits one of three things:
the adulterer, male or female, who has previously been in a valid marriage; the killer of an inviolable soul, who is killed under the conditions for the death penalty;
and the apostate from the religion who separates from the community of the Muslims by leaving Islam and its rites, whether or not he joins other religions, by openly declaring that he has left Islam.

So every Muslim should guard his religion, his blood and his wealth, and keep away from these prohibited things, for a severe threat in the Hereafter has come for whoever commits one of them, besides the apostate being judged a disbeliever. We ask for safety and well-being from every affliction and trial.
Keep all your limbs from indecency; / they will be your best witness on the Day of Recompense.
